Subject: Sizing follow-up: microburst tolerances & KV cache boundaries

Lara,

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday — excited by the product fit. A few quick follow-ups so we can convert your workload profile into a preliminary dedicated sizing sketch:

1) Could you attach a small sample of production telemetry (CSV) for a 24–72 hour window if possible? Ideally rows with timestamp, request_type (chat/completion), prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id, latency_ms.

2) One-off numbers that help sizing: baseline QPS, observed peak-burst QPS, typical burst duration, percentage of requests that call external tools (function-calls), and percent of long-tail responses (>1k tokens).

3) For session affinity: average session life (seconds), and proportion of sessions that are multi-turn vs single-turn.

Operational constraints we should be aware of: p99 latency target (if you have one), required region/data residency, and any hard upper bounds on commit size for the first 6 months.

Attached is a short questionnaire (redwood-dedicated-questionnaire.pdf) with the fields we typically use for a first-pass estimate. If you can drop an anonymized sample CSV we can run it through our sizing heuristics and come back with an initial fleet proposal (GPU types, pool size, burst buffer recommendation).

Plan: once we have sample telemetry, Marissa will do a modeling pass and Karthik can validate assumptions about session tiling and KV cache sizing.

Cheers,

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Sean — thanks, attaching the 48h sample as requested (acme_traffic_sample.csv). High level numbers from our ops team so you have context:

- Baseline steady-state QPS: ~12 qps
- Observed extreme microburst peak QPS: ~480 qps (duration ~30–60s; happens 2–3x/day during ad-hoc campaigns)
- Typical burst shape: sharp ramp 2–3s, plateau 20–60s, exponential fall 10–30s
- Avg prompt tokens: 58
- Avg response tokens: 302
- Long-tail responses (>1000 tokens): ~1.4% of requests
- Multi-turn sessions: ~72% (avg turns per session = 5.2)
- Avg session duration: 75s (median 48s)
- Function-calling rate: 12% of requests (mostly small JSON payloads)
- Streaming: ~78% of responses streamed client-side
- P99 latency target for interactive queries: 450 ms (we try to keep interactive flows sub-500ms)
- Data residency: US-West primary; backup EU not acceptable for primary workload

Procurement contact copied here: procurement@acme-ai.com for contract and PO steps. Let me know if you need additional columns in the sample CSV (we can add user-id hash and call trace id).

Lara Chen
Head of Platform Ops

On Wed, Jul 28, 2026 at 5:03 PM Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme-ai.com> wrote:
> Sean — thanks, attaching the 48h sample as requested (acme_traffic_sample.csv). High level numbers from our ops team so you have context:
> - Baseline steady-state QPS: ~12 qps
> - Observed extreme microburst peak QPS: ~480 qps (duration ~30–60s; happens 2–3x/day during ad-hoc campaigns)

Lara — thanks for the quick data. I ran a first-pass model on the sample and want to call out the assumptions so we can align:

Assumptions used for the draft sizing math (attached as initial-sizing-math.xlsx):
- Model selection: flagship open LLM (gpt-open-13B equivalent) with quantized path; throughput reference = ~1.2K tokens/sec per A100-80GB when running optimized kernels and batching.
- Effective token rate per request = prompt_tokens + response_tokens * streaming_overhead (we used 1.05 to account for tokenization + transport).
- Concurrency mapping: we map session concurrency to GPU slots using average active tokens/window. Multi-turn sessions with KV cache reduce duplicate work; we model a KV cache hit-rate of 58% for repeated context within a session.

Preliminary recommendation (conservative, to meet p99=450ms):
- Initial dedicated pool: 6x A100-80GB (reserved), region: us-west. This assumes autoscale + burst buffer of +3 GPUs (autoscale policy to add capacity within 30s for sustained increases).
- Burst buffer sizing: allow ephemeral burst capacity to handle 480 qps spikes (we size based on token/sec and burst duration; see spreadsheet).
- KV cache: shard capacity per GPU ~14–18GB for session caching; recommend enabling prefix cache for authenticated sessions to reduce token cost.
- Fallback policy: configure an immediate fallback to a smaller 7B-equivalent model for tail latencies and graceful degradation for non-critical endpoints.
- Observability: enable token-level traces for 72h after go-live to validate assumptions then tune occupancy/oversubscription.

Open questions we flagged in the sheet:
1) Are the microbursts fully latency-sensitive (i.e., do they require p99=450ms) or can part of them be degraded to best-effort? Even moving 20% of tail QPS to best-effort reduces required reserved capacity by ~25%.
2) For function-calls: are the external calls synchronous on your critical path (i.e., do we need to provision for remote call latency inside GPU SLO)? If yes, we need representative remote call latencies.
3) Any hard budget constraints for committed GPUs in Q1? This affects whether we recommend 6 reserved vs 4 reserved + larger burst buffer.

I'll sync with Karthik on session tiling specifics (he has a note on KV cache faulting pattern that could materially change shard sizing). If this looks plausible, Sean — can I propose we schedule a 45-minute sizing review next Tuesday with your ops and procurement to confirm the pilot configuration and run a 30-minute stress window?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marissa — really helpful, thanks for the clear assumptions and the sheet. A few quick answers: 

- Microbursts: ~85% of those are customer-facing and require the interactive latency SLO. We can tolerate best-effort for internal analytics calls.
- Function-calls: synchronous on the critical path for ~70% of those 12% calls. Average external call latency ~80–120 ms (third-party enrichment).
- Budget: procurement prefers a staged commit (4 reserved GPUs first month, auto-expand to 6 if telemetry aligns). They want a 90-day pilot cadence.

We can do the 45-minute sizing review next Tue (Aug 3) 10:00 AM PT and run the stress window immediately after (ops will stand by). Procurement will join to discuss the staged commit.

Talk Tuesday — thanks again.
